title: Accelerating ab initio melting property calculations with machine learning: application to the high entropy alloy TaVCrW

recollection.intervention: Guess: Use of machine learning to accelerate ab initio calculations of melting properties
recollection.structure: Guess: Focus on the atomic structure and phase behavior of TaVCrW alloy
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Machine learning models trained on ab initio data to predict melting points and related properties
recollection.results: Guess: Machine learning significantly reduced computational cost while maintaining accuracy in melting property predictions for TaVCrW; quantitative results likely include predicted melting temperatures and comparison to traditional ab initio methods

score.note: The recollection only restates the title-level idea of using machine learning to accelerate melting calculations. It omits the specific MTP-for-liquid and FEP-for-TI substitutions, the <1 meV/atom training error and phase-space fidelity, the FEP variance/convergence mechanism, electronic and SRO contributions, and all reported numerical results such as 80% savings, 193/160 K deviations, 48/57 K shifts, and 2.4 meV/atom stabilization.
